questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you press the brakes
The distance your vehicle travels from when a hazard appears until you see it
The distance your vehicle travels before you decide to brake
The distance your vehicle travels from when you press the brakes until it stops

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you press the brakes
questions.explanation: Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you physically press the brakes.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce how well your vehicle can brake.
Work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
Do not work well on large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside your vehicle's regular brakes. It does not increase or decrease your braking power. ABS only turns on when your wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to move away from your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy need special permits. Drivers of these loads must follow special rules, such as driving only at certain times.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Let off the gas and push in the clutch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let off the gas and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down by letting off the gas and pushing in the clutch.

questions.question: Using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Gives you better control when braking hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you better control when braking hard.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control of your vehicle when braking hard. However, it does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure causes a loud bang or heavy thumping and vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear of your vehicle fishtails, stop and check your tires. Smoother steering is not a sign of tire failure.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. Texting takes your mind and your hands off driving.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or every three hours.
Only after going up a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or every three hours.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. You are responsible for keeping your cargo safe and secure the entire trip.

questions.question: When covering cargo, a cover that flaps while driving:
questions.explanation: A cargo cover should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover your cargo. It can also block your view or other drivers' views.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Should not be used on any vehicle.
Should not be used on the front of a bus.
Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Crashes from tired driving happen more often at night than at any other time.

questions.question: Drowsy driving happens most during:
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most at night because people are naturally less alert during hours when they normally sleep. If you must drive at night, take steps to prevent tired driving.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. The surface looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable. The meat swings while the truck moves, and its center of gravity is high.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. If you wear eyeglasses, keep them clean and unscratched. Make sure you are rested and alert before driving at night.

questions.question: What may happen if the exhaust system is not working properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may exit the rear of the muffler system.
It may cause problems if the trailer is fully loaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes enter the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine work properly:
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Antifreeze helps engines work well in both cold and hot weather.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used with caution because:

options.text: There may be fuel spilled on the ground that could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares if the weather is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: There may be fuel spilled on the ground that could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires after accidents often happen from using flares near spilled fuel. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The total weight of a vehicle before cargo
The maximum weight allowed to be transported by a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of the vehicle and everything loaded in it.

questions.question: After a vehicle is started, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn off quickly. If a light stays on, it means something is wrong with your vehicle.

questions.question: When alley docking, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, pull past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area.

questions.question: What must be done before transporting an over-length load?

options.text: Alert fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads require special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions use double clutching to shift gears. This skill requires practice.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose. If you see rust near the wheel nuts, check that they are tight before driving.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, look under the vehicle to check for:

options.text: Whether the vehicle is on an incline.
Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
Whether the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: When approaching your vehicle, check its general condition. Look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 inch

questions.explanation: Check that front tires have tread depth of at least 4/32 inch and other tires have at least 2/32 inch. Tires must not be cracked or worn too much and must be the same size. Different brands are acceptable, but all tires should have proper air pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem to avoid?

options.text: Using radial and bias-ply tires together
Using recapped tires on the front of a school bus
All tires are made by the same company

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires are made by the same company
questions.explanation: During inspection, check for low or high air pressure, excessive wear, cuts or damage, tread separation, dual tires touching each other or the vehicle, mismatched sizes, radial and bias-ply tires together, damaged valve stems, and regrooved or recapped tires on the front wheels of school buses.

questions.question: If using air tanks with manual drains, how often should you drain the tanks?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems with manual drains should be drained at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Vehicles driving behind a truck:

options.text: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
Often have a great view of the roadway in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have difficulty seeing objects in front of the truck.
questions.explanation: A truck blocks the view of drivers behind it. They cannot see hazards ahead that might require you to stop. Flash your brakes and warn other drivers before you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To avoid blocking traffic while driving a heavy vehicle, you should:

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match the speed of other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: How is water and compressor oil removed from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out of the tank.
A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil from the tank.
The water and oil are removed automatically as the brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to remove the water and oil from the tank.
questions.explanation: Open a drain valve to remove water and compressor oil from air storage tanks. This buildup can damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads where traction is poor. Slow down by about one-third of your normal speed.

questions.question: If air pressure drops between ____, a visual low pressure warning signal should already be on.
questions.explanation: The visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a truck cab due to:

options.text: The wrong type of fuel being used.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Without the proper amount of oil in the engine:

options.text: A vehicle will have difficulty stopping.
A vehicle will make quick, jerking movements while being driven.
The engine may be quickly damaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine may be quickly damaged.
questions.explanation: An engine needs adequate oil pressure to work properly. An engine can be destroyed quickly if it runs without oil.

questions.question: To put out an electrical fire, use:
questions.explanation: B and C type fire extinguishers work on electrical fires. Never use water on an electrical fire because it can cause electric shock.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab due to:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A faulty exhaust system is a serious safety hazard. Poisonous fumes can enter the vehicle's cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If you see a vehicle with a distracted driver, you should:

options.text: Maintain a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and keep a safe following distance.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, hydroplaning happens more easily if your tires do not have enough air pressure or if the tread is worn down. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Look ahead on the road ____ in front of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot dangers and react to them. Look for vehicles entering the highway, moving into your lane, or turning.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be fixed, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Problems with the suspension are very dangerous.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up
Stop a vehicle from speeding up on hills
Stop a vehicle from speeding up downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) prevent the wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when you press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Brake lights are controlled by an electric switch that turns on when you press the brake pedal. Air pressure triggers this switch to turn the lights on.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means the ABS:

options.text: Cannot work because of the weather.

questions.explanation: When the ABS light comes on, something in the anti-lock brake system is not working properly.

questions.question: One way to avoid being an aggressive driver is to:

options.text: Use your cell phone while driving.
Judge how other drivers are driving.
Plan for a realistic travel time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan for a realistic travel time.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. This helps reduce frustration that leads to aggressive driving. Also drive at a safe speed, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and avoid making rude gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: In very hot weather, you may need to:

options.text: Drive faster to cool the engine.
Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.
Follow other vehicles more closely than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to prevent the engine from overheating.
questions.explanation: Driving faster creates more heat in the engine and tires. Slow down in hot weather to avoid overheating.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous gases into the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous gases into the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can allow dangerous gases to enter your vehicle. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop soon to:

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
Check that the tire has enough air.
Check that you changed the right tire.
Check that changing the tire did not damage another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to make sure the wheel nuts are tight.
